evidence.text: Peers that reported after ACCV's IPO all showed data-center power demand accelerating in the September quarter: Vertiv (10-28) Americas sales +66% organic, organic orders >100%, FY26 sales guide raised $650M; Eaton (11-03) Electrical Americas data-center sales +54%, rolling-12M orders +39%, backlog +33%; nVent (10-30) sales +44% and FY organic guide raised to 38-39%, but orders grew only low double digits and Q4 is guided down to 26-29% on supplier capacity. ACCV's sell-side models were built off the roadshow before any of these prints.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No usable history: this is ACCV's first print as a public company, and the sweep marked the baseline history untrustworthy. For the peers, Vertiv rose 16.5% on its 10-28 beat-and-raise (https://www.trefis.com/stock/vrt/articles/623340/what-is-behind-the-drop-in-vertiv-stock/2026-11-06), then gave it back in the 11-04/05 policy selloff.
evidence.why_not_priced: ACCV's price has moved on the sector's political risk, not on its demand. It fell 17% on 11-04 and to $9.95 on 11-05 along with Vertiv (-13%, then -14%) after the midterms and the Texas governor-elect's moratorium pledge. If the peer demand read were priced, ACCV would not be at 25x a FY26 EPS that S&P's eight analysts set in late October, below every initiating target ($16-22). The five initiations of 10-26 predate Eaton's 11-03 print.
evidence.independence: Three separate companies and documents. Eaton: https://finviz.com/news/414001/eaton-reports-record-third-quarter-2026-results-with-strong-organic-growth-accelerating-record-orders-and-backlog-raises-organic-growth-guidance (2026-11-03). nVent: https://finviz.com/news/412747/nvent-beats-and-raises-again-but-lagging-orders-and-a-q4-slowdown-keep-the-bulls-on-the-defensive (2026-10-30). All three are proxies (peers), not ACCV's own number.

evidence.text: The company's own prospectus shows backlog of $1,111M at 2026-06-30, up from $419M at 2025-12-31, with book-to-bill of 3.5x for Q2 and 2.5x for H1. That covers the ~$464M H2 revenue implied by FY26 consensus of $901.7M about 2.4 times, which makes a Q3 revenue shortfall from lack of work unlikely. The cap: the Q3 bar is unsourced, and the tight consensus range ($898-904M) suggests the models are anchored to management's roadshow framing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for ACCV (first print). The rule 'a prospectus backlog implying bookings far above what previews anchor on' has paid in this repo's resolved days [sizing note removed], but here the consensus already sits near the backlog-implied run rate.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced. The backlog is public, but the stock trades at about $2.9B total equity value (225M shares x $12.8) against about $4.0B at an IPO that was itself priced below range. A market that believed the backlog converts on schedule, with the Q3 book-to-bill still above 1, would not have sold the stock 29% below the IPO price on political risk alone. What the print adds is the Q3 book-to-bill and the end-September backlog, which no aggregator carries.
evidence.independence: Same company document as the gross-margin finding (the 424B4), but a different line (backlog and bookings rather than margin). The peer orders in finding 1 point the same way; that is a different source.

evidence.text: The prospectus shows gross margin compressing: about 26.6% for H1 2026 against 30.4% for H1 2025 and 32.3% for FY2025 (computed from the S-1 summary table). A post-IPO note attributes this to higher labor costs and project inefficiencies, and the S-1 risk factors name field rework, commissioning delays and change-order risk. If Q3 margin stays in the mid-20s while revenue beats, the quality of the beat is poor.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No ACCV history. Peers set the comparison: Eaton's Electrical Americas margin was 29.8% (+230bp sequentially) and Vertiv's adjusted operating margin 25.2% (+290bp), so the sector is expanding margin while ACCV's was contracting.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced, which is why the size is small. The compression is in the prospectus and in tickeron's 10-20 note. The FY26 EPS consensus of $0.50 on about $900M of revenue already embeds thin margins. If the market expected the compression to reverse, the stock would not trade 29% below the IPO price, and if it expected it to worsen, the 8 analysts would not all have Buy or Hold ratings.
evidence.independence: https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-accelevation-holdings-accv-stock-down-4-00-today-19916/ (2026-10-20) cites margin pressure from labor costs and project inefficiencies. That is a secondary read of the same S-1, so it is partly the same document.

evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as a sector read. It is a proxy: ACCV's customers are not named, and nothing confirms Microsoft or IREN as a counterparty. It stays unpriced only to the extent the call reveals that a top-two customer slipped its schedules.

evidence.text: On 10-09 ACCV refinanced its January 2025 MidCap Financial credit agreement with a Bank of America-led $250M Term Loan A and $400M revolver: SOFR+2.25%, maturity 2031, $150M drawn, leverage covenant 4.0x from Q1 2027. What the money buys is a lower-cost bank facility plus revolver capacity for working capital against a $1.1B backlog. That is a ramp, not distress, and lower interest expense helps the Q4 and FY27 EPS framing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 2.55% on the 10-13 announcement (StockTitan), on a day of sector weakness.
evidence.why_not_priced: The interest saving is an inference: the 8-K does not state the old facility's margin, and a MidCap private-credit facility is typically priced well above SOFR+2.25%. The Q3 P&L will show the first partial-quarter effect, and the FY guide will show the run-rate. If the saving were in the models, the FY26 EPS range ($0.42-0.56) would already sit higher relative to net income.
evidence.independence: None beyond the same 8-K; the size is small for that reason.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise drew opposite reactions. Q3 2025 (2025-11-12): revenue $46.3M against about $42.0M estimate, a 10% beat, with a raise; stock -13.4%. evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus sits mechanically at the guide midpoint and is low on sequential growth. If the market had fully priced a large raise, the sell-side targets would sit above spot rather than about 15% below it, and the skew would not be +32 for puts.
